# Server-rendered Blog Posts at Real URLs — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Server-render each blog post at a slug-based URL (`/blog/<slug>/`) and server-render the `/blog/` list page, so blog content becomes crawlable, shareable, and indexable.

**Architecture:** Add a `slug` field to `BlogPost` (auto-generated, backfilled via data migration). A `blog_detail` view renders Markdown→sanitized HTML at `/blog/<slug>/` with per-post SEO tags (title, meta description, canonical, Open Graph, `BlogPosting` JSON-LD). The `/blog/` list view is converted from JS-fetch to a server-rendered, paginated template whose cards link to the real post URLs. Homepage cards keep using the JS/API path (with a `slug` added to the API response).

**Tech Stack:** Django 5.2, PostgreSQL/pgvector, `markdown`, `nh3` (HTML sanitizer), Docker.

---

## Test harness (READ FIRST — all test commands below depend on this)

There is **no host-reachable database** (the `db` container publishes no port) and the `web` image bakes code at build time. So tests run **inside the container against the compose network**, with the working tree bind-mounted so code edits take effect without a rebuild.

One-time per session:

```bash
cd /home/bigaddict/Projects/Codebases/brantech-full-website
docker compose up -d db        # bring up Postgres+pgvector (healthy)
```

Run tests with this exact form (mounts live source, overrides the gunicorn entrypoint with `python`):

```bash
docker compose run --rm \
  -v "$(pwd)/brandtechsolution:/app/brandtechsolution" \
  --entrypoint python web \
  manage.py test brand.tests_blog -v 2
```

Notes:
- New Python dependencies (`markdown`, `nh3`) live in the **image**, not the mount — so Task 1 (which adds them) requires `docker compose build web` before any test that imports them.
- The Django test runner creates/destroys a `test_brantech` database on the `db` container and applies all migrations (the pgvector image provides the `vector` extension).
- New tests live in a focused new module `brand/tests_blog.py` to stay clear of the repo's pre-existing (separately broken) `brand/tests.py`.

- [ ] **Step 4: Create the migration** `brandtechsolution/brand/migrations/0009_add_blog_slug.py` with three operations (add nullable → backfill unique slugs → enforce unique). Hand-author it exactly (do NOT rely on `makemigrations`, which would emit a single unique AddField that fails on existing rows):

```python
from django.db import migrations, models
from django.utils.text import slugify


def backfill_slugs(apps, schema_editor):
    BlogPost = apps.get_model("brand", "BlogPost")
    for post in BlogPost.objects.all():
        if post.slug:
            continue
        base = slugify(post.title)[:200] or "post"
        slug = base
        n = 2
        while BlogPost.objects.exclude(pk=post.pk).filter(slug=slug).exists():
            slug = f"{base}-{n}"
            n += 1
        post.slug = slug
        post.save(update_fields=["slug"])


class Migration(migrations.Migration):

    dependencies = [
        ("brand", "0008_remove_blogpost_brand_blogpost_created_idx_and_more"),
    ]

    operations = [
        migrations.AddField(
            model_name="blogpost",
            name="slug",
            field=models.SlugField(max_length=220, null=True, blank=True),
        ),
        migrations.RunPython(backfill_slugs, migrations.RunPython.noop),
        migrations.AlterField(
            model_name="blogpost",
            name="slug",
            field=models.SlugField(max_length=220, unique=True, blank=True),
        ),
    ]
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `brandtechsolution/brand/markdown_utils.py`:

```python
"""Render user-authored Markdown to sanitized HTML safe for direct output."""
import markdown as _markdown
import nh3

_ALLOWED_TAGS = {
    "p", "br", "h1", "h2", "h3", "h4", "strong", "em", "b", "i",
    "ul", "ol", "li", "a", "code", "pre", "blockquote", "hr", "img",
    "table", "thead", "tbody", "tr", "th", "td",
}

_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES = {
    "a": {"href", "title", "rel"},
    "img": {"src", "alt", "title"},
}


def render_markdown(text: str) -> str:
    """Convert Markdown text to sanitized HTML.

    Single newlines become <br> (nl2br) so legacy plain-text posts keep their
    line breaks. Output is sanitized against an allowlist, so raw HTML such as
    <script> or event-handler attributes is stripped.
    """
    if not text:
        return ""
    html = _markdown.markdown(text, extensions=["extra", "nl2br", "sane_lists"])
    return nh3.clean(html, tags=_ALLOWED_TAGS, attributes=_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES)
```

Replace the existing `blog` view with:

```python
def blog(request):
    """Blog list page (server-rendered, paginated)."""
    post_list = BlogPost.objects.all()  # Meta orders by -created_at
    paginator = Paginator(post_list, 9)
    posts = paginator.get_page(request.GET.get("page"))
    return render(request, 'brand/blog.html', {'posts': posts})
```

Add the detail view (anywhere after `blog`):

```python
def blog_detail(request, slug):
    """Server-rendered individual blog post at /blog/<slug>/."""
    post = get_object_or_404(BlogPost, slug=slug)
    BlogPost.objects.filter(pk=post.pk).update(view_count=F('view_count') + 1)
    content_html = render_markdown(post.content)
    return render(request, 'brand/blog_detail.html', {
        'post': post,
        'content_html': content_html,
    })
```
